standard_prerequisites.name: The derived pushforward is computed on an object by choosing a K-injective representative and taking the pushforward of that complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Defines the functor whose equivalence with the pushforward to the structure sheaf is proved.

standard_prerequisites.name: A K-injective complex of quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme is described by the corresponding statement so that the pushforward can be compared sheaf by sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the compatibility needed to view the pushforward as a functor to modules over the pushforward of the structure sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: On affine schemes the equivalence between modules over the structure sheaf and over the pushforward of the structure sheaf is the standard one, and pullbacks of quasi-coherent modules remain quasi-coherent
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to the affine case and shows the comparison functor is an equivalence there.

standard_prerequisites.name: Higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules vanish for an affine morphism, which makes the comparison with the derived pushforward an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the composition of the equivalence with the pushforward to the structure sheaf with the derived pushforward.

core_obligations: Recall how the derived pushforward is computed, choose a K-injective representative of the object and define the functor to modules over the pushforward of the structure sheaf by pushing forward that representative (proof lines 940-950).

Compare the two categories: the pushforward of the structure sheaf is a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras, and the standard equivalence between the module categories over the two sheaves of rings is compatible with the functors involved (proof lines 950-965).

Reduce to the affine case, where the equivalence is the usual one between modules over a ring and modules over the pushforward along an affine morphism, using that pullbacks of quasi-coherent modules stay quasi-coherent (proof lines 966-985).

Use the vanishing of higher direct images for an affine morphism to see that the composition of the obtained equivalence with the functor to the quasi-coherent derived category of the base is the derived pushforward, which is the second assertion (proof lines 985-989).
proof_roadmap: Define the functor via K-injective representatives (proof lines 940-950).
Compare the categories over the two sheaves of rings and reduce to affines (proof lines 950-985).
Identify the composite with the derived pushforward using relative affine vanishing (proof lines 985-989).
